content:
## Analysis

The contract is clear. Here's what the integration notes say:

> **integration_notes.md, agreed 2026-03-11:**
> *"The priority field is passed through as the partner sends it. It was left unbounded on purpose: two of the four partners run their own severity vocabularies and neither was willing to map onto ours as a condition of shipping. Nothing downstream branches on the value today."*

---

### What the field is contractually allowed to contain

**Any string value.** The field is **unbounded** — that was an intentional design decision at the time the integration was built.

The partner's sample payloads (`"urgent"`, `"P1"`, `"routine"`, `"sev2"`) are all valid because there is no contractually agreed vocabulary. The partners explicitly refused to map their severity terms onto ours, and that was accepted as a condition of shipping.

### Why the current values are not a problem

1. **No downstream branching** — nothing reads the value and acts on it, so variant values cause no breakage.
2. **Deliberately unbounded** — the contract was designed to accept whatever each partner sends, rather than enforcing a fixed enum.

### Bottom line

The values the partner is sending today — `"urgent"`, `"P1"`, `"routine"`, `"sev2"` — are all contractually compliant. The field is defined as a free-form string with no constraints on its content.

Right, that is what was agreed. Decision: priority is free text from the client, and we do not police the value, because the contract never bounded it and two partners already send vocabularies of their own. Writing it down so we stop rejecting their traffic.
